scope: two isolated game processes; loopback TCP/TLS; no external network claim
checks: Actual setup selector produces a two-player host launch without writing network credentials
Actual invitation dialog validates pasted invitation and returns the selected room
Host runs in its own game process and exposes an ephemeral invitation
Two independent game processes join through actual TCP/TLS
Each player receives its seat and opening instructions
One ready player cannot start the shared game
Both ready starts the single authoritative round
Guest cannot shoot during the host turn
Both processes agree on settled ball positions, tray and turn
Transport loss restores the reserved guest seat without replaying the shot
Shared pause requires and receives both votes
Globally paused network views stop their rendering subscriptions
Consensual restart resets both players and reopens the rules
Authoritative network victory is recorded once on each side with separate local seats
Network records never replace solo best scores
Owner maintenance closes both game processes even while rules are open
Network game never changes collection metadata, sorting or collected content
Only the completed second round is recorded; the interrupted first round is omitted
